alternatives_rejected.why: Pure delay would raise latency uniformly with few errors. Instead, the error metric is by far the largest deviation (z=11088765.6), and p90 (33597.8%) rose much more than p50 (2777.8%). That pattern fits retransmission-driven tail latency from loss (E1, E4).
Memory did deviate (z=207.23), but it is orders of magnitude smaller than the error and latency deviations (E4). It looks secondary, for example from buffered retries, rather than the primary fault.

Its latency-90 deviation (z=3936.91) is smaller than productcatalogservice's (z=6719.57), and no error deviation is listed for it (E1). That is consistent with latency inherited from its productcatalogservice dependency.
It has no significant metric deviation (E1), and the worst failing traces end at productcatalogservice (E3). That suggests it only propagates the downstream errors.

proposed_fix.description: Remove the network impairment on the productcatalogservice pod or node (for example, clear any tc/netem loss rule on its interface) and check its network path. If the impairment cannot be found, reschedule the pod onto a healthy node. Then confirm that the error rate and p90 latency return to baseline.
